newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products slide in line with crude.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products slide in line with crude.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were softer on Wednesday, traders said.
Gasoline was weaker in line with NWE and U.S. markets which fell heavily.
Traders said that the market was tighter than in northern Europe following heavy buying during the French strike, but prompt demand was now weak.
"There is no big demand," said one trader.
Premium unleaded cargoes were assessed around $217 a tonne cif Med.
Heating oil remained long and premiums were under pressure at cif high flat to -$0.25 basis Genoa, down $1/1.50 from the start of the week.

A cargo of 0.5 percent sulphur heating oil was rumoured done fob Lavera high $1.25 for possible movement to India, but some traders described the price as unusually firm. Traders continued to explore an arbitrage to India. Physical trade in low sulphur diesel was dull.
Fuel oil could not resist the pull of plummeting crude and prices fell. Activity was slow with buyers holding back in the hope of further losses tomorrow.
High sulphur cracked material was pegged in the low teens cif while low sulphur was knocked to below $140 cif Med.
"Material is available from the U.S. and NWE and no one looks to have bought," said one dealer.
